subject: Chemistry
title: The Reaction That Makes Steel
description: One-minute skill: The Reaction That Makes Steel.

hook.text: Iron is soft and rusts easily. Add a tiny amount of carbon and it becomes steel—stronger than almost anything.

buildup.text: For centuries, making steel was slow and expensive. Only swords and small tools justified the cost.

discovery.text: Henry Bessemer's 1856 process blew air through molten iron. Oxygen burned away excess carbon in minutes.

twist.text: Cheap steel transformed everything: railroads, skyscrapers, bridges, ships, cars, and canned food.

climax.text: The world produces 1.9 billion tons of steel per year. Civilization is literally built on this reaction.

punchline.text: Blow air through molten iron. Minutes later: steel. Cities followed.

quiz.question: What does the Bessemer process do to turn iron into steel?
options: Blows air through molten iron to burn away excess carbon
Adds more carbon to make iron harder
Cools iron rapidly in cold water

details.summary: Steel production relies on the basic oxygen process, which blows pure oxygen through molten pig iron to oxidize excess carbon, silicon, and manganese. This controlled oxidation reduces carbon content from about four percent to less than two percent, transforming brittle iron into versatile steel.
details.whyItMatters: Steel is the most used metal on Earth, fundamental to construction, transportation, and manufacturing. The chemistry of steelmaking determines the material properties of modern civilization.
takeaways: Steel is iron with carefully controlled carbon content below two percent
Oxygen blasting removes excess carbon through oxidation
Different carbon levels produce steels with different properties

faq.question: Why does reducing carbon content make iron stronger and more flexible?
faq.answer: Excess carbon in cast iron forms brittle graphite inclusions that crack under stress. Reducing carbon allows iron atoms to form a more uniform crystal lattice that can deform without fracturing, giving steel its characteristic blend of strength and flexibility.

faq.question: What is the difference between carbon steel and stainless steel?
faq.answer: Carbon steel contains mainly iron and carbon, while stainless steel adds at least ten percent chromium to form a protective oxide layer. Carbon steel is stronger and cheaper but susceptible to rust. Stainless steel sacrifices some strength for corrosion resistance.
